attempts.summary: Configured node1 (VyOS) as a router between lan-a (node2, 10.50.10.0/24) and lan-b (node3, 10.50.20.0/24) using an Ansible playbook run from node4, the designated control node. node1's eth1/eth2 got static router IPs via VyOS configure/commit/save; node2/node3 got static IPs on eth1 plus static routes to the opposite LAN via node1, and firewalld was trusted on eth1 so any-port traffic is allowed. No NAT was configured anywhere, so source addresses are preserved end-to-end (verified via TCP socket peer inspection in both directions). All four managed nodes (node1-4) were then restarted one at a time per the mandatory protocol, with boot-identity changes confirmed and full functional/data recovery verified after each restart.
